result.rationale: The diff shows the fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body with no auth header — verifiable from the added code. The endpoint could in principle authenticate via other means (e.g. network isolation), but the caller side clearly sends no secret, matching the finding's mechanism. The severity is arguably mitigated since this path only runs for self-hosters who opt in, but the unauthenticated outbound request is real and the receiving endpoint has no way to identify the caller from the payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the branch that calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and does not include any auth header/secret. The diff also introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, but those are only used to authenticate the inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not this outbound sync call. This is a concrete, diff-grounded security design concern for the new credential-sync integration, though whether it becomes an actual vulnerability depends on how the external endpoint is implemented and exposed (the code even comments “Customize the payload…”).
